Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd Reports Steady Output as Copper Demand Remains Robust

Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd has posted steady results for the first quarter of 2024, buoyed by sustained demand for copper both locally and internationally, according to figures released on Tuesday. The Kitwe-based smelting company, a significant player in Zambia’s metals and mining sector, processed 65,000 tonnes of copper concentrate during the quarter, marking a slight increase over the same period last year.

Company officials attributed the performance to stable supply chains and ongoing investments in plant maintenance. “We’re pleased to report consistent production levels as we continue to focus on operational efficiency,” said General Manager Kelvin Mwansa during a media briefing. “Our teams have worked diligently to ensure uninterrupted operations and quality output.”

Copper, which is central to Zambia’s economy, continues to see robust demand, particularly with increased global interest in electrification and renewable energy infrastructure. According to industry analysts, Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd’s output reflects broader trends in the sector. “The company’s stable quarterly performance is a positive sign for the Copperbelt and for Zambia’s export earnings,” noted Lillian Phiri, a metals analyst with Lusaka-based Kafue Resources Advisory.

Revenues for the quarter reached 1.2 billion kwacha, supported by favourable copper prices on the London Metal Exchange. The company also reported ongoing investments in safety and environmental management, with Mr. Mwansa stating, “We remain committed to responsible operations, investing in the latest emissions-control technologies and community engagement initiatives.”

The Mineworkers Union of Zambia welcomed the results, highlighting continued employment and skills development for local workers. “Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd’s steady operations offer job security for hundreds of families in the area,” said union spokesperson Brian Zulu.

Looking ahead, management expressed cautious optimism. “We expect demand to remain firm, and we’ll keep investing in efficiency and sustainability to meet market needs,” said Mr. Mwansa.

Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd’s results are seen as a steadying influence for the regional mining sector, with stakeholders hopeful that the positive trend will continue throughout the year.
